name: BigCommerce
description: Read-only BigCommerce store access: store profile, catalog products, orders and customers

tools.name: list_products
tools.description: List BigCommerce catalog products (id, name, sku, price, stock level, visibility)

tools.name: list_orders
tools.description: List BigCommerce orders (Orders V2) with status, total and customer id

tools.name: store_info
tools.description: Get the connected BigCommerce store's own profile (name, domain, currency, plan, status)

needs_review: base_url is the object/template form "https://api.bigcommerce.com/stores/{{store_hash}}" (NOT the brief's ".../v3"), because this store mixes API versions: catalog products and customers are V3 while orders and the store profile are V2 (/v2/store is exactly the endpoint the vault registry's live-tested testEndpoint uses, services/auth/config/integrationTypeRegistry.js key 'bigcommerce'). A /v3 base_url could not express /v2/store at all. The version prefix therefore lives in each tool path.

store_hash is a vault credential field, so it rides in the PATH. A wrong or absent store hash makes every subpath unroutable: verified by curl 2026-09-12, store hash 'qx9shapeprobe' answers an openresty HTML 404 identically at /v2/store, /v3/catalog/products, /v2/orders, /v3/customers AND at the control path, with no JSON envelope at all. The blind harness reads an HTML 404 that matches its control as path_wrong, so with an unknown hash the whole spec would report FAIL for a reason that is not a wiring defect.

base_url._probe substitutes store_hash = 'n0i50vy', which is BigCommerce's OWN Cornerstone theme demo store (hash read from the cdn11.bigcommerce.com/s-n0i50vy asset URLs on https://cornerstone-light-demo.mybigcommerce.com/, 2026-09-12), not a merchant's store. With that hash the API surface routes: every tool path answers 401 {"status":401,"title":"Unauthorized",...} while the control path answers 404 {"status":404,"title":"Not found",...}, so the differential is real. The probe is read-only with a dummy token and the runtime ignores _probe entirely.

Orders uses V2 (/v2/orders), the documented list-orders endpoint. /v3/orders also routed (401 rather than the control's 404) on 2026-09-12, so a V3 orders surface exists, but which V3 order operations are list-capable is UNVERIFIED and V2 is what the REST docs list for this. Caveat for consumers: V2 /v2/orders answers 204 No Content (empty body, no array) when a store has no matching orders, so an empty result is not an error.
Category set to 'commerce_finance' to match the shipped taxonomy (stripe, shopify, square, paddle); the scaffolded 'ecommerce' is not a bucket any shipped spec uses.
static_headers Accept: application/json is declared because the V2 API is content-negotiated; the V3 endpoints answer JSON regardless. Same pattern as postmark and intercom.

Every response pick comes from the REST documentation (tools_source), not from a live 2xx: no BigCommerce store was held for this draft, so field names, the V3 {data, meta.pagination} envelope and the V2 top-level array shape are documentary. list_products deliberately picks inventory_level rather than a variant-level stock figure, which is per-variant and not present on the product row.
